title: Misinformation Monthly – November
summary: Each month, Cyabra's experts share the articles, reports, and investigations shaping the conversation around misinformation, narrative intelligence and deepfakes. This September, from AI chatbots buckling under sustained misinformation pressure to the growing legal fight against deepfake harm, one thing is clear: as generative AI reshapes how false narratives are created and corrected, distinguishing reliable information from AI-amplified falsehoods is more critical than ever.
body_markdown:
**Each month, Cyabra’s experts share the articles, reports, and investigations shaping the conversation around misinformation, narrative intelligence and deepfakes. This November, from AI tools generating election deepfakes on demand to new research exposing the commercial pipelines behind synthetic abuse, the conversation is moving past reactive moderation toward targeting the underlying infrastructure that enables deception at scale.**


### [To end ‘whack-a-mole’ war on AI deepfakes, address the ‘ecosystem,’ researchers urge](https://www.brown.edu/news/2026-11-09/ai-deepfake-legislation)


**Brown University**


“We need to shift our focus to the technical infrastructure enabling and profiting from this abuse. In order to protect vulnerable communities online from the various types of harms and emotional distress that can come from this form of abuse, we must first see this ecosystem clearly.”


— Michelle Ding, Ph.D. Student, Brown University


### [AI-driven disinformation running rampant on social media before US midterms, experts warn](https://www.theguardian.com/us-news/2026/oct/27/ai-disinformation-social-media-midterm-elections)


**The Guardian**


“You can run an information operation now with quality that was impossible in 2016 for super, super cheap… because you can just keep tweaking the post a little bit each time you create them, and some of them are going to get through.”


— Frances Haugen, former Facebook data engineer and whistleblower


### [Weaponized Uncertainty: Deepfakes, Democratic Resilience and the Scandinavian Test Case](https://www.international.ucla.edu/institute/article/299407)


**UCLA International Institute**


“Professional communicators absorb the epistemic cost on behalf of publics who never see the transaction, which makes the sexualized targeting of women in public life an attack on democratic infrastructure rather than on individual reputations.”


### [LLMs Are Still Making Election Deepfakes Just Days Before the US Midterms](https://www.techpolicy.press/llms-are-still-making-election-deepfakes-just-days-before-the-us-midterms/)


**Tech Policy Press**


“Every AI tool that we tested produced convincingly false content.”


— Abdiaziz Ahmed, technology policy strategist, Brennan Center for Justice


### [8 Tactics Foreign Actors Used To Influence the 2026 Midterms](https://www.fdd.org/analysis/8-tactics-foreign-actors-used-to-influence-the-2026-midterms/)


**Foundation for Defense of Democracies**


“In 2024, AI mostly helped adversaries scale content. This cycle, operators began using it to run the operations. Foreign actors are deploying AI agents that create fake accounts, generate political content, and spread it with limited human oversight.”


— Jacob Breach & Pavneet Kaur, Foundation for Defense of Democracies (FDD)
